html:
SMTO-GWT-0063 — SMTO isn't allowed to change this GPU's settings

GUID: beec7983-78d0-53e2-9d1e-8e62f4280447
Slug: gpu-permission-denied
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The computer account that SMTO's Gateway runs under doesn't have permission to change graphics card settings, so the card refused the change. No GPU settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell the person who manages the computer with the GPU that the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands there) needs permission to change NVIDIA GPU settings. Changing power, speed or modes on NVIDIA cards needs system rights that only an administrator of that computer can grant.
  2. Don't type an administrator or root password into the conversation to get around this. SMTO doesn't store root passwords or add admin commands for GPU changes; the permission has to be set up on that computer.
  3. After the administrator confirms the permission is in place, ask SMTO to make the GPU change again. The card refused the change before it happened, so asking again is safe once permission exists.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the GPU change as done, and the GPU details show the new value.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't share a root password with SMTO or store one in its settings as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • nvidia-smi returned its permission-denied exit code (4): the OS account running the Gateway lacks NVIDIA configuration privileges.

What this means

  • The NVIDIA provider returned its permission-denied exit classification for the Gateway OS account. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The NVIDIA provider returned its permission-denied exit classification for the Gateway OS account.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the account and requested NVIDIA operation, preserving current authorization and avoiding disclosure of private credentials.

How to fix it

  • Grant the OS account that runs the Gateway the privileges nvidia-smi needs for configuration on that host (the Gateway capabilities readiness for GPU states 'Gateway OS account must have NVIDIA configuration privileges'). SMTO never elevates, uses sudo or stores a root password; configure the privilege deliberately on the host, then repeat the request, since exit code 4 is classified as not executed.
  • Ask the operator to configure appropriate Gateway OS privileges; do not store a root password or invent sudo commands.

Retry and execution caution

  • Ask the operator to configure appropriate Gateway OS privileges; do not store a root password or invent sudo commands.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation is permitted under deliberately configured OS privileges and its result is verified.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
